metadata.title: How does PISA define and measure reading literacy?

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA in Focus brief describes the conceptual framework and assessment design for PISA 2018 reading literacy rather than reporting an original student-level statistical analysis. It states that PISA 2018 was delivered in 79 countries/economies and that a new reading framework was adopted for computer-based delivery, including adaptive testing and multiple-source tasks. Because no analytic model, estimation procedure, or variance estimation method is presented, the manuscript does not specify whether complex survey weights or replicate weights were applied. For users working with PISA microdata, the standard practice is to apply the provided student/sampling weights (and replicate weights when variance estimation is required) to account for the multistage sampling design; however, this brief itself does not provide the weight variable names or any weighting decisions.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a framework/definition brief that explains how PISA defines and measures reading literacy (including multiple-source reading and reading fluency) but does not report an empirical model that uses PV-based achievement outcomes. As a result, plausible values handling and missing-data handling strategies for PV estimation are not applicable to the content presented here. The brief also does not provide methodological details on missingness treatment because it is not conducting a new analysis on microdata.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The brief does not define an analytic subsample for an empirical analysis. It reports that PISA 2018 reading was delivered on computer in 70 education systems and that over 600,000 15-year-old students participated across 79 countries and economies; it does not specify exclusions (e.g., missing background variables, task non-completion) or any restriction to a particular grade band beyond the PISA target population (15-year-olds).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA in Focus brief explains the PISA 2018 reading literacy definition and how the assessment operationalizes it. It emphasizes that reading literacy involves understanding, using, evaluating, reflecting on, and engaging with texts to achieve goals, develop knowledge and potential, and participate in society. The 2018 framework was updated to reflect digital reading, with greater emphasis on multiple-source reading: tasks use texts composed of multiple units created by different authors or at different times, and computer delivery enables navigation tools such as hyperlinks or tabs. The brief also notes that reading fluency is assessed via sentence-level coherence judgments and that adaptive testing targets items to students’ ability levels for more precise proficiency measurement. It provides illustrative examples (e.g., the “Rapa Nui” unit) showing that students must compare information across sources, integrate information to form inferences, evaluate credibility, and handle conflicts across texts.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse because the document is not an empirical ML study and does not report an analytic sample, model specification, or performance metrics. It functions as an assessment-definition and framework description for PISA 2018 reading literacy, so fields related to PV handling in estimation, missing-data treatment, and ML techniques are not part of the reported methodology. Consequently, main_findings and confounders_identified are intentionally empty because no predictive targets or statistical controls are analyzed in this brief.
